angles.drive: You built your own standard with no one watching. Making a thing yourself feels safer than being measured on it, so you build alone rather than with help. Let one favour into the making, since you pay most for the things you make alone.

angles.cost_others: Making everything yourself is what you show a new peer first. By making each thing alone instead of sharing it, you leave your peers nothing to carry. Hand one piece over, because all you take from them is the chance to matter to you.

angles.drive: You hold everyone to the same measure as yourself. Fairness feels cleaner to you than favour, so being even with someone comes ahead of being easy on them. Let a friend off the hook sometimes, since you keep everyone you measure at a distance.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a friend falls short of the measure, you keep the measure rather than the friend. Holding everyone to one even standard is how you stay honest. Bend it once for someone you like, because you spend long stretches without company that fits.
angles.cost_others: Being even-handed with a friend is how you show respect. You hold people you like to your own measure, and hand them your standard ahead of your warmth. Offer the warmth first, as you cost them the ease of being liked without being graded.

angles.drive: Your strength recovers alone and gets spent in company. Being seen low feels like a debt you never repay, so you recover quietly instead of calling anyone. Let one person near while you are low, because you recover slower alone than you need to.

angles.cost_others: Recovering alone spares the people near you your worst days. You return recovered rather than being seen recovering, and give them the finished version only. Let them in on one of those days, since you deny your closest people the chance to be needed.

angles.drive: You stay sealed off long after the reason has gone. There is Metal to spare in you, so you seal yourself off from help without noticing whether you want any. Keep in mind that you seal out the closeness as much as the risk.
angles.cost_self: A hurt is the first thing you seal off, before anyone notices. Needing no one proves you are fine, and you keep it sealed instead of letting help in. Do not forget that every sealed hurt costs you evenings you could have shared.
angles.cost_others: Sealing everyone off politely keeps you easy to live with. You give them calm with nothing under it, your sealed quiet ahead of their wish to come in. Remember that you leave them loving a version of you that never needs them.

angles.drive: Being taught lands on you as an attack first and information second. With Metal running over, you put your own judgment ahead of any peer's lesson. It is worth remembering that you are only taught by someone you let be right.
angles.cost_self: Whenever someone tries to teach you, you check the messenger first. Since being right is how you stay safe, you defend a position rather than learn from it. You lose, remember, every lesson that needed you to be wrong before it could teach you.
angles.cost_others: Teaching the people around you comes easier than being taught. Your standard sits above theirs by default, and you hand out the fix ahead of the question. Bear in mind what you take from your peers, the chance to be right now and again.

angles.drive: Asking once costs you more than doing a thing twice yourself. Metal is heavy in you, so asking reads as failure and carrying alone reads as proof. Notice how you count the asking as the cost and never the carrying.
angles.cost_self: Where a job is heavy, you take it all instead of asking for half. To prove you are enough, you carry it alone and spend sleep before spending one question. As you know, you pay in lost sleep for help you never ask for.
angles.cost_others: Being nobody's burden is why you ask no one. Since you would rather owe nothing than be joined, you take the job back the moment someone offers. Spare a thought for the peer you send away with an offer still in hand.

angles.drive: You compete best with someone to beat and know it. Knowing where you stand matters more than comfort, so you compete harder against one rival than for any reward. Pick one contest with a finish line, because yours have no end in sight.
angles.cost_self: Without a rival, you lose your pace. Competing keeps you going, and the next round comes ahead of noticing you are tired. Compete against your own record for a month, since you never reach a finish that lets you rest.
angles.cost_others: For you, competing with a friend is taking them seriously. You raise the stakes out of wanting someone worth beating more than someone easy to keep. Keep one friend outside the contest, as you cost a rival the ease of siding with you.

angles.drive: Your yes to a bet comes before the fear has finished. Hesitating feels like losing to yourself, so you bet first and size it afterwards. Keep one bet a year you can afford to lose, since nerve costs you money as much as pride.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the stakes go up, you are first to bet. Betting first is the closest you get to sure, and you size it to nerve rather than savings. Size one bet to the savings, because the early yes costs you money put aside.
angles.cost_others: Betting first is your way of carrying the people who hesitate. By betting for the group instead of asking it, you put their money where your nerve is. Check the size with them first, before you spend their caution like your own courage.

angles.drive: You trust a person faster when the risk is shared. Sharing the risk makes the bond real to you, so you go in together ahead of writing anything down. Write the terms down once, because you risk the friendship as much as the money.
angles.cost_self: Where a friend needs backing, you share the risk first. Sharing the risk feels closer than staying out, and the shared bet comes before your margin. Keep one account no friend can draw on, since you cover their losses with money meant for rest.
angles.cost_others: Sharing a risk with someone is your warmest offer. Wanting them in it more than safe from it, you share the upside and the fall. Say the downside first, as you bring the people you like into risks sized to your nerve.

angles.drive: You keep an exact score with everyone you like. With Metal running over, you live on comparison more than company, so you keep a quiet tally of who gave more. Remember that you started counting to be fair and kept counting to be ahead.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a friend pulls ahead, you score it as a loss rather than their win. To stay sure, you keep score and spend the friendship checking the count. Do not forget that you pay for every point in closeness you never collect.
angles.cost_others: Keeping the score even is how you keep a friendship honest. Since you count favours instead of returning them, you hand the people you love a bill. Be honest with yourself that you turn their gifts into debts without telling them the price.

angles.drive: Your bets are sized to the thrill ahead of the margin. Metal piles up in you, so your bets run on nerve to spare and caution borrowed. You bet the rent, and you know it, on a feeling that fades faster than the bill.
angles.cost_self: Where the bet is biggest you are calmest, and read it as a sign. Trusting nerve more than math, you bet with the rent before the sums are done. You pay for that calm later, as you know, in rent and sleep.
angles.cost_others: Betting the rent is how you make a thing feel real. Since you size the bet to your nerve instead of theirs, you pull the people beside you into it. Weigh how much of their safety you bet along with your own each time.

angles.drive: Harder than any loss deserves, you hate to lose. You read a loss to a peer as a statement about you, so you argue the result instead of taking it. You hate losing your place, if you are honest, more than losing the point.
angles.cost_self: Coming second sours the whole day for you. Being beaten feels like being replaced, and you hate the loss rather than learn from it. You give the loss the entire evening, remember, and get neither the rest nor the lesson back.
angles.cost_others: Hating to lose even a game is how you show you care. Since you want the win ahead of the evening, you keep arguing after it ends. Keep the people you play with in mind, because you cost them the fun of the game.

angles.drive: A finished thing gives you a calm that starting never does. Since a half-done piece sits with you like an open promise, you finish one thing properly rather than start three. If you keep the list short, you get to finish all of it.
angles.cost_self: Finishing comes before enjoying for you. A thing is not yours to like until it is done, and you finish the gift ahead of the pleasure of making it. Leave one thing half done this week, and notice how much rest comes back to you.
angles.cost_others: Every gift you give, you finish alone. The making feels like part of you, so you finish it yourself rather than with the person it is for. When you finish the last step together, you hand them a share in the making.

angles.drive: Choosing the right thing to give is how you care. A wrong gift feels worse to you than none, so you choose slowly rather than give the nearest thing. Once you set yourself a deadline to choose, you reach the person while it counts.
angles.cost_self: For you, a good choice beats a fast one. Since getting the choice right matters more to you than being on time, you let the warm moment pass. Choose a little faster for the people you love, so you get the closeness you were after.
angles.cost_others: You choose kind words as carefully as gifts. Anything plain sounds careless to you, so you choose silence rather than say something plain to someone you love. Each time you choose the moment along with the words, you let them hear the warmth you feel.

angles.drive: Showing how a thing is done comes more easily to you than explaining it. You trust your hands over your words, and teach by doing it next to someone rather than telling them. Stay beside the learner, and you pass on the thing itself.
angles.cost_self: Teaching by doing takes your time twice, since you would rather do a thing beside someone than write it down. You teach that way even where a note would do. Teach one lesson by note to keep an hour of rest.
angles.cost_others: You teach a child by doing the whole thing yourself. Your own way is the one you know works, so you teach it rather than let them try another. Whenever you teach only the first step, you let them find a way of their own.

angles.drive: Pleasing you takes exactness. A thing has to be right in every detail before it pleases you, and you check the small part rather than enjoy the whole. Keep in mind that while you hold out for perfect, you go without being pleased at all.
angles.cost_self: Being hard to please costs you the pleasure. Since your pleasure has to be earned, you hold it back rather than enjoy what is only nice. It is worth remembering that you never get back an evening spent waiting to be pleased.
angles.cost_others: You look a gift over before you let it please you. You put the flaw ahead of the thanks, and keep the maker from seeing you pleased. You give a maker the most when you let the gift please you first.

angles.drive: Giving is how you know you are here. The made thing in someone's hands proves you more than anything kept, so you give what you made away ahead of keeping any of it. Remember to count yourself among the people you make things for.
angles.cost_self: Giving too much leaves you with the least. Since keeping a thing for yourself feels mean to you, you give the best one away rather than hold on to it. It pays to remember how much rest you give away with every gift.
angles.cost_others: When you love someone, you give before they ask. Giving feels more natural to you than keeping, so you hand over even the things you need. By giving it all, you leave the people you love no chance to look after you.

angles.drive: Taking it easy comes naturally to you. Because what you make comes out well without much effort, you stay with what you do well rather than learn what you do badly. Bear in mind that you never try the hard parts while taking it easy.
angles.cost_self: Your best work is what taking it easy costs you. What comes easily feels like enough, and you enjoy the version you have instead of reaching for the one beyond it. You have the better piece in you already, and only effort gets it out.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you take it easy, you take people with you. Because your first try looks finished, you show them stopping rather than pushing, and hand them good enough as the ceiling. Do not forget that you teach them by what you settle for.

angles.drive: Saying it straight is the only way you know. A softened truth feels like a lie with manners to you, and you name what is wrong ahead of smoothing it over. Say it early as well as straight, so the truth costs you fewer friends.
angles.cost_self: Being straight costs you the welcome. Because being right out loud matters more than comfort to you, you say the unsaid thing and lose a few invitations. If you let a small wrong thing pass, you keep the friends worth being right for.
angles.cost_others: Whenever something is wrong, you say so before you say anything kind. Being exact feels more honest to you than being gentle, and you hand people the mistake ahead of the credit. Once you lead with the credit, you make the mistake easier to hear.

angles.drive: Setting the bar is something you do unasked. A standard you did not choose bores you, so you set your own rather than keep the given one, and hold yourself to it. Set it high for the year, lower for the day, and reach both.
angles.cost_self: You never rest under a bar you set yourself. Because the standard is yours, you raise it rather than meet it, and the mark moves each time you near it. Set one bar you are allowed to clear this month, and enjoy the clearing.
angles.cost_others: When you set the bar, you set it for everyone near you. Your standard feels more honest than a shared one, and you hold the people beside you to a mark they never chose. Call the bar yours to let them choose it.

angles.drive: Being watched brings out your best work. A thing done unseen feels half real to you, and you perform with someone watching rather than practice alone. When you find a small audience for the dull parts, you do them as well as the show.
angles.cost_self: Your best needs a witness. With no one there to rise for, you let the private hours go slack rather than drill them, and the talent that grows unseen stays small. Record one practice a week, and you give the quiet hours an audience.
angles.cost_others: You save your best for an audience. A crowd feels more worth rising for than one person, and you perform for strangers ahead of the people at home. Whenever you give the people at home a show, you keep your best where it is loved.

angles.drive: Direct is the only setting you have for the truth. A softened answer feels like a lie you would have to keep up, so you say it exactly rather than gently. Being this direct, you make a fair point land harder than it has to.
angles.cost_self: Direct talk costs you people who would have stayed. Being right counts for more with you than a welcome, so you say the hard thing and lose easy company. Remember that you lose the company you came for each time you say it that directly.
angles.cost_others: You hand people your read in its plainest, most direct form. Plain truth feels like respect to you, so you skip the soft words rather than soften the point. Keep in mind that you leave them a bruise the truth alone would not have left.

angles.drive: Talking back comes first in you. A rule you did not agree to feels like being pushed around, so you talk back rather than ask what it is for. It helps to remember that you waste your talking back on small rules.
angles.cost_self: You talk back hardest to the people who correct you. Because being corrected feels like being made small, you talk back to whoever could teach you instead of learning from them. You win the back-and-forth and leave the lesson behind.
angles.cost_others: Given a task by a teacher, you talk back first. Since the last word guards your pride, you would rather talk back than get on with it. Do not forget that you spend a little of their patience on every small fight.

angles.drive: Grading people is something you do without meaning to. A quick read of someone's worth feels safer than not knowing, so you grade them on sight rather than wait to be surprised. It is worth remembering that you grade yourself the same way.
angles.cost_self: Grading someone costs you what they know. Since you would rather be right about a person than learn from them, you stop listening at the grade. Bear in mind how little you learn from anyone once you have graded them.
angles.cost_others: When you meet someone, you grade them before you greet them. The fast read feels more honest than the slow one, and you give people the grade instead of your attention. Try to remember how rarely you let someone change the first grade you gave.

angles.drive: You spot the opening when it is only a gap. You wake more for a far chance than a near one, and you spot a newer opening while you are claiming this one. You pay in openings taken halfway, and one taken whole repays you.
angles.cost_self: Spotting the opening comes easier than staying for it. You spot to feel ahead, and once the opening is yours you look out again rather than down into it. Take one spotted chance through to the money, since those you leave open close without you.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you spot an opening, you tell the partner building this one with you. You spot the next one ahead of this one out loud, and your partner hears the plan move. You cost them a week of building toward somewhere you spotted and left.

angles.drive: Fast starts are your natural speed. You feel most alive in the first week, and this is why you start the next venture rather than sit through this one. Staying through one middle is where your fast start turns into money.
angles.cost_self: Where you feel surest is starting fast. You start on speed alone, while you would rather spend your patience on a fresh start than a middle. You never get paid by what you keep starting over, and the money waits at the end you skip.
angles.cost_others: Starting fast means starting for other people too. Since you start before your partner has agreed, you put your speed ahead of their say. You hand them a venture already moving and leave them a month of catching up to a start they never made.

angles.drive: Giving freely is what you do first with what comes in. You feel money belongs to whoever needs it next, and you give it on rather than set it aside. You give best from a kept share, and the unkept share is the price.
angles.cost_self: Keeping is harder for you than giving freely. You would rather give money on than sit with it, since holding still feels like being stuck. You end up with nothing saved for the year you need it, because you never give to yourself.
angles.cost_others: With the people around you, giving freely is how you stay close. You give to the newest friend more freely than to the oldest one, since newness is what moves you. You leave the ones at home with what is left after the giving.

angles.drive: The move you trust most is moving on. You need the next place in view to feel free, so you move on at the first slow week rather than stay. Keep in mind that each venture you move on from cost you something to start.
angles.cost_self: Always moving on is how you avoid being pinned. You would rather move on to somewhere new than be found at the old venture, even with money still in it. You already know moving on leaves more money behind than new ventures bring in.
angles.cost_others: Moving on, you leave people as well as plans. You move on and put the next place ahead of those who built the last one with you. Bear in mind that your partners start over each time you move on, and only you chose it.

angles.drive: Spread thin is how you like it. You feel most at ease with several ventures open, and you spread yourself across all of them rather than into one. It is worth remembering that spread thin leaves you thin where you most wanted to be.
angles.cost_self: Spread thin, you never learn what you could do whole. You stay spread over shallow ventures rather than deep in one, since the one you skipped always looks better. Spread thin, you pay in rest never taken and the one venture that would have paid.
angles.cost_others: Spreading yourself thin spreads your partners thin with you. You spread your attention over every venture instead of down into one, and each partner gets a slice. You signed each of them up for all of you, and spread thin you show up in slices.

angles.drive: Spending it all is your first instinct. You feel money that sits is a chance going cold, and you spend it all on the next thing rather than keep it. It helps to remember that spending it all leaves you empty-handed for the next chance.
angles.cost_self: Deciding what to keep is harder than spending it all. You spend to feel money move rather than sit, since a sum held still feels like a missed chance. Spent out, you come up short for the one opening that asks for cash up front.
angles.cost_others: Where you are generous, you spend everything too. You spend it on the bill, the gift and the loan, since giving suits you better than keeping. The thing to remember is that you spend what your family counts on for later.

angles.drive: Finishing things settles you more than starting them. You carry an open task until it is closed, so you finish what you hold ahead of starting anything new. Finish as you do, and let one thing stay open long enough to grow.
angles.cost_self: Proof that you are reliable comes from finishing things. You finish whatever is nearest rather than whatever matters most, since finished is the feeling you are after. You lose your rest to small finishes while the one that would pay waits.
angles.cost_others: For other people, you finish things too. You finish the last steps of a shared plan rather than wait for your partner, since waiting feels like leaving it undone. You finish their half with yours and take from them the small pride of closing it.

angles.drive: Your reflex with money is saving first. You feel a sum set aside cannot be lost, so you save rather than spend, and spend only what is left. You save your way past small pleasures too, and one sum spent uncounted buys one back.
angles.cost_self: Saving first keeps the fear of having nothing away. You put the saving ahead of what it was for, and you move the wanting to later. You pay for saving first with a life kept for later, and you cannot bank the years.
angles.cost_others: You save first for the people you love as much as for yourself. You save for a shared future rather than spend on a shared present, and call that love. You put the evenings you saved through into a future your partner never asked for.

angles.drive: Keeping your word matters more than being liked. You carry a promise like a debt until paid, so your word gets kept ahead of your way out. You keep your word honest by asking once whether it is still wanted.
angles.cost_self: Changing your mind is harder than keeping your word. Your word stays kept past its reason rather than broken, since breaking it dents how steady you feel. Where it still counts, keep your word, because you pay for the rest in years inside outgrown promises.
angles.cost_others: Where your word is kept, you expect it back. You hold the person you love to a word given in another mood rather than let it go. Your word, kept for both of you, costs your partner a wish they were never allowed to say.

angles.drive: Your answer to ownership is holding on tight. You would rather hold on than risk losing, so you hold on to money, things and people past where holding helps. You hold on tightest to the things you no longer want.
angles.cost_self: The fear of loss goes quiet while you are holding tight. You keep hold of the savings rather than spend them on their year, since spending feels exposed. Holding on costs you trips not taken, with the money outliving its purpose.
angles.cost_others: Holding on tight reaches the people you love too. You hold a partner the way you hold a sum, close and counted, rather than let them go. You leave the person beside you no air when you hold on this tight.

angles.drive: Your default with cost is playing it safe. You feel a loss more than a gain the same size, and you play safe for the small sure return rather than the big one. Playing safe costs you too, slower and in money you never count.
angles.cost_self: Playing it safe keeps you out of the loss column and the win column. You take the known small wage rather than the unknown better one, since playing safe is never judged. You pay for playing it safe in the chance you watched another take.
angles.cost_others: For the ones you love, playing safe is the rule too. You keep a partner on the safe plan rather than their wanted one, since their risk feels like yours. Never forget that the safe life you play for is only half yours to keep.

angles.drive: Keeping what works means avoiding change. You know the price of what you have and not of the better, and you keep the known rather than try a change. Long after the known stops paying you, you go on avoiding change.
angles.cost_self: Avoiding change spares you being new at anything. You keep the steady job and the steady love after they stop feeding you rather than change either. Avoiding change costs you the better life you never tried.
angles.cost_others: Where you avoid change, you avoid it for two. You keep the person you love inside the agreed life instead of letting them change it. You avoid change so well that your partner goes without any too.

angles.drive: Taking charge comes to you before anyone asks. A crisis gives your force a charge to carry, and you carry it yourself rather than wait for someone else to step up. Let someone else take charge sometimes, since always leading means never being carried.
angles.cost_self: Whenever something goes wrong you are already in charge. You would rather hold the charge than trust it to anyone, and the load stays yours by choice. Hand one charge over this month, because the rest you skip is a price only you pay.
angles.cost_others: In trouble that is not yours, taking charge is your first move. You take the charge ahead of being asked, and the people near you give up their own decisions early. Leave one charge unclaimed, since the people you lead need practice too.

angles.drive: Pressure is where you do your best work. A real stake lets you thrive where comfort lets you drift, and being tested suits you better than being at ease. Keep thriving on it, and notice that nothing without pressure gets the same care.
angles.cost_self: Under pressure you become the self you trust most. Calm holds nothing to thrive on, and you take one more load rather than sit through a quiet week. Give yourself one empty day, since thriving charges you in rest you never take.
angles.cost_others: You expect everyone near you to thrive on the pressure you do. Stakes bring out your best, and you set pressure on others ahead of asking whether they wanted any. Ease the pressure sometimes, since those you push pay in calm they lose.

angles.drive: Deciding fast is how you stop a crisis from deciding for you. A quick decision points your push somewhere, and you accept being wrong early rather than being right too late. Keep the speed, and give one slow decision its day sometimes.
angles.cost_self: Fast decisions are the ones you trust. Deciding quickly keeps you ahead of the crisis, and you take the first good option rather than the best. Sleep on one decision a month, because the better option you never saw is what speed costs you.
angles.cost_others: When someone near you is stuck, you decide for them. You settle it in one fast decision rather than wait, and those close to you lose the chance to choose. Hold one decision open, because the people you decide for pay with their say.

angles.drive: Being hard on yourself is a rule you never had to learn. Every standard turns into a judge in you, and you fail your own hard test sooner than pass someone else's. Keep in mind that you answer to no judge harder than yourself.
angles.cost_self: Under any load, you go hard on yourself first. You take the blame hard and ahead of the credit every time, since your standard never relaxes. Bear in mind that being this hard costs you credit never claimed and rest never taken.
angles.cost_others: The hardness you keep for yourself sets everyone's rate. Your mistakes feel unforgivable, and being hard on people near you comes easier than letting one pass. You take their ease with every mistake your hardness refuses to pass, and it helps to remember that.

angles.drive: Even on days nothing is asked of you, you stay on duty. Being needed is the only rest you trust, and you pick the next duty rather than the night off. Remind yourself that you are the one keeping you on duty.
angles.cost_self: Off duty is a state you never fully manage. The alert in you never stands down, and you spend a free evening on duty rather than inside it. You pay for the duty in rest never taken, a price worth holding on to.
angles.cost_others: Staying on duty is how you look after people. You stand duty over their troubles ahead of sitting with them, and the people you guard get a guard in place of company. Hold on to this much, that coming off duty is allowed.

angles.drive: Pushing too hard is your answer to anything slow. Your own pace is the only safe one, and you push ahead of asking if the push was wanted. Take note that you are using force with every push, whether you mean it kindly or not.
angles.cost_self: You pay more for every push than the thing you pushed does. Stopping feels like falling behind to you, and you push on rather than refuel. You live in the body you push, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_others: Your care comes out as a hard push. You push loved ones toward their good ahead of asking, and those closest to you get force in place of patience. Keep patience in view, since it costs you less than the push.

angles.drive: Keeping your word is the standard you hold above every other. A promise is a rule of your own making, and you would rather carry a hard yes to the end than give an easy maybe. Enjoy that, and let a few promises stay small.
angles.cost_self: Once given, your word outranks your own change of mind. You would rather be stuck in a promise than break it, and you remain long after it stopped fitting. Renegotiate one promise, since the way out you never take is what trust costs you.
angles.cost_others: The word you keep is the one you quietly expect from everyone. A promise binds you, and you hold people to their exact words ahead of their meaning. Give them the looser reading sometimes, because your word holds whether theirs is exact or not.

angles.drive: Doing it properly is the only way you know. A rule gives your effort a shape, and you follow the proper procedure rather than any shortcut. Enjoy that your work holds, and allow one job a draft instead of the proper version.
angles.cost_self: Properly is the one speed you own. You do every step properly rather than good enough, and small tasks take the care big ones deserved. Let one thing be good enough, since the hours you never get back are what properly costs you.
angles.cost_others: With everyone near you, properly is the standard. Procedure matters more than pace to you, and you send work back for its improper step ahead of thanks. Lead with thanks sometimes, because your standard holds whether the proper step comes first or last.

angles.drive: Earning your place counts for more with you than being handed one. Rank only feels earned when the rules gave it, and you choose the slow route rather than the shortcut. Keep earning it that way, and let yourself accept the occasional gift.
angles.cost_self: Slowly earned is the only place you trust. An early title feels unearned, and you wait for the rules to promote you rather than put yourself forward. Ask once this year, since the step never asked for is what earning slowly costs you.
angles.cost_others: Each time someone rises near you, you check the place was earned. An unearned rank looks wrong to you, and you credit people for the record ahead of the talent. Credit the talent too, since your eye for the earned sees half a person.

angles.drive: Needing permission comes before wanting, in your order of things. A rule outranks a wish in you, and you wait to be allowed rather than take what is yours. Keep sight of this, that you are the one not giving the permission.
angles.cost_self: Permission is the thing you wait for most. A move without permission feels like a mistake, and you hold back at the door rather than walk through it. You pay in chances closed while waiting to be allowed, and that bill deserves remembering.
angles.cost_others: You pass the need for permission to anyone under you. Permission from above is the only yes you take, and you send their questions up rather than answer. You leave them waiting on permission you were free to give, a wait worth remembering.

angles.drive: Hating being wrong is the part of you that works hardest. A mistake marks your name in your eyes, and you give silence in place of any answer that risks being wrong. You would do well to remember that being wrong out loud is allowed.
angles.cost_self: Being wrong is what you have no procedure for. Right answers feel like the only safe ones, and you hold opinions back rather than risk being wrong. You pay in ideas never said for fear of being wrong, a price to hold on to.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a correction comes, hating being wrong slows you. A correction feels like a charge, and you defend the answer ahead of hearing where it went wrong. You cost those near you the right to call you wrong, and that right is worth remembering.

angles.drive: Putting rules first is how you stay steady. A rule asks nothing of your judgement, and you follow it rather than read the person in front of you. Keep this with you, that you hold the rule and the rule does not hold you.
angles.cost_self: Rules come first with you, even ones that hurt. Breaking a rule feels like losing standing, and you stay inside a dead rule rather than step out. You pay in standing a rule kept you from, and the bill is worth keeping in view.
angles.cost_others: Unsure of someone, you put the rule first. A rule treats everyone the same, and you apply it ahead of the person's case. Each time the rule goes first, you take their hearing, and that is the thing to keep in mind.

angles.drive: You test everything before you let it in. A fact only becomes yours once tried against something real, and that puts testing ahead of simply learning. Keep the slow filter, and what you know stays yours for good.
angles.cost_self: Testing everything costs you time. Slow and sure means more to you than quick and wrong, so most of your learning starts late. Let one good teacher skip the test, because every hour spent proving the known is an hour not spent learning the new.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone hands you a fact, you test it in front of them. Trying it yourself matters more than being agreeable, and whoever offered it gets a question instead of thanks. If you test it later in private, you keep both fact and goodwill.

angles.drive: You are rarely fooled. Being fooled by a person costs you more than being slow to trust one, so you weigh the uneasy feeling ahead of the proof. When a kind person proves your doubt wrong, being fooled by kindness is a loss worth taking.
angles.cost_self: Rarely fooled, you are slow to be glad. You check an offer for the catch before letting it near, and would rather miss a good thing than be fooled. Once you take an offer at its word, you get back what your doubt sends away.
angles.cost_others: You check an honest word as closely as a false one. Being hard to fool counts for more with you than being easy company, and you make a truthful person prove it twice. You keep more honest company with every first answer you let stand.

angles.drive: Your best thinking happens alone. You need quiet for a half-formed idea more than an audience, so you shut the door until it is whole. Each time you bring one person in at the halfway point, you keep the quiet and lose only the loneliness.
angles.cost_self: Thinking alone keeps the idea clean. You would rather carry a hard question alone than let anyone see it unsolved, and help only reaches a problem someone has heard about. Once you tell one person early, help you have done without starts arriving.
angles.cost_others: Your thinking stays private until it is a result for others. Working it out alone comes easier to you than together, and the people near you get only the conclusion. When the door opens earlier, you give them a say in the deciding.

angles.drive: You are never done checking. Letting a thing out early feels like a mistake you cannot undo, so you check once more rather than hand it over. Remember that you stopped finding errors long ago and now check for comfort.
angles.cost_self: Checking a thing again feels safer than handing it in. You would rather send it late and right than early and good enough, and the late ones mostly never go. You lose more chances to the extra check than to the errors it catches.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone asks, you reply only once the answer is fully checked. Late sits easier with you than wrong, and you leave whoever asked waiting on your standard instead of your reply. You owe them a rough version now more than a right one later.

angles.drive: Precision matters to you past the point of being followed. A near-enough answer feels like a small lie to you, so you give the precise one rather than the easy one. Most days you get one of exact or understood, and one is enough.
angles.cost_self: Being exact costs you people who talk loosely. You correct a small error in a story rather than let it land, and over time fewer people tell you much. You wanted to be told more than you wanted it exact, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_others: Handed a rough idea, you give it back exact. You would rather fix the wording than hear what it was for, and the one who brought it gets a correction instead of a reply. You were handed it for hearing, and grading was never asked.

angles.drive: Hard to reach is what you become mid-thought. You need it whole before anyone touches it, so you let messages wait rather than answer half-minded. You get the thought back more easily than the person, and that fact is worth keeping.
angles.cost_self: Being hard to reach keeps the thinking clean and the evenings empty. You would rather answer a thought than a person, and over time you get asked less. You give up closeness for the quiet, and every call you let ring out proves it.
angles.cost_others: Reaching you means waiting for a thought to finish first. You put the unfinished idea ahead of the person at the door, and your silence lands as the answer. Each time you give the minute first, you find the thought waiting when you come back.

angles.drive: Whatever you are told stays with you. Being a safe place is how you know you matter, so you keep a confidence rather than ever use it. Let someone keep one of yours in return, because you wear thin with nothing kept for you.
angles.cost_self: Keeping a confidence means carrying it. You hold what people tell you rather than talk it through with anyone, and the weight of other lives sits on your own rest. Give one of them to a notebook, and you keep the trust and the sleep.
angles.cost_others: You keep your own troubles as closely as everyone else's. You would rather hold things than need holding, and you give the ones who tell you everything nothing of yourself back. Once you hand one of them a worry, the shelter becomes shared.

angles.drive: You learn a thing properly or not at all. Half-knowing a subject bothers you more than not knowing it, so you go to its end before counting it learned. When you take the slow way on purpose, what you learned stays true under pressure.
angles.cost_self: Learning it properly takes you longer. Knowing a thing to its end matters to you more than knowing it well enough, and most chances ask for less. Once you take one door on less than the whole, you stop watching chances go to faster people.
angles.cost_others: Teaching waits until you have learned it properly. You would rather pass a subject on whole than in pieces, and the people learning from you get nothing before the whole arrives. The more you teach as you learn, the less knowledge you keep from them.

angles.drive: You steady people by holding them to something. Keeping someone safe matters more to you than keeping them comfortable, so your care arrives as a standard rather than a hug. When you put the warm word before the rule, your steadying lands as love.
angles.cost_self: Steadying people earns you respect ahead of closeness. Being needed when things fall apart suits you more than being phoned for nothing, and the no-reason calls are what you miss. Once you rest the standard an evening, you get the closeness it stands in for.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone arrives to be held, you steady them instead. A standard feels more useful to you than a kind word, and you hand the one who came for comfort a lesson. Each time you ask what they need first, you keep the steadying wanted.

angles.drive: You stay the student long after you were able to teach. Learning under someone suits you more than standing alone, and that keeps your seat in the back row past its use. You decide when the student turns teacher, and you keep putting it off.
angles.cost_self: Staying the student keeps you safe and small. You would rather stay under what you are learning than stand on what you know, and staying asks nothing of you. Remember that you lose the place meant for you to someone who felt ready sooner.
angles.cost_others: Your door stays closed while you stay the student. You keep your knowledge under another's wing rather than make one of it, and the ones who need your shelter stand outside. Every year as the student, you keep a shelter from people who needed it.

angles.drive: Protective is your instinct with the people you love. You need them safe more than you need them tried, so you step in ahead of letting them fall. You are protecting them from the one thing that would have taught them, and you know it.
angles.cost_self: Being too protective costs you your sleep. You carry every risk your family should carry themselves, and you choose tired ahead of watching them hurt. Bear in mind, you trade your own rest for a lesson they never get to learn.
angles.cost_others: Your protective side keeps the ones you love from finding their feet. Catching them matters more to you than letting them learn, and you take one lesson from them with every rescue. You give them safety where they wanted faith, and faith was cheaper.

angles.drive: You love people by correcting them. Getting someone right feels like caring to you, so you fix the small wrong thing rather than sit with the whole sad one. Keep in mind that you are correcting someone who only came to be loved.
angles.cost_self: Loving by correcting costs you the ones who stop bringing things. You put being useful to someone ahead of being close to them, and the corrected learn to bring you only finished things. You get respect for it, and the closeness goes somewhere less exact.
angles.cost_others: Correcting is what you give people wanting comfort. You would rather set people straight than let them be, and you send them home taught instead of held. Each time you hold a lesson back, you let through the warmth it stood in front of.

angles.drive: On your own terms, you set a bar and trust it more than any outside grade. Each time you clear it, you set it a little higher. If you leave it in place for a week, you get the satisfaction you keep putting off.
angles.cost_self: Where you set your own bar, you set it alone. Since no one else's standard moves you, you stay steady while you skip the help a peer would give. Let a peer check the bar sometimes, and you win back the help you walk past.
angles.cost_others: The bar you set for yourself travels to everyone beside you. Because you never say it, you expect a match rather than ask for one. Say the bar out loud once, and you give the people beside you a fair chance to meet it.

angles.drive: You need no backup, and owing no one is how you feel safe. You trust yourself as backup more than anyone you could call. Go without backup only where it counts, because you need your strength for those days.
angles.cost_self: Without backup you never learn what being covered feels like. You give that relief far more than you accept it, since accepting would mean admitting a need. When you let yourself need backup, you get back the rest you have been doing without.
angles.cost_others: Standing without backup keeps the people who would stand behind you at a distance. You would rather owe nothing than let a friend in, and that leaves them nothing to hold. Call on a friend as backup once, to show them they count.

angles.drive: Whatever the week brings, you hold steady. Calm is what you trust, and you hold steady instead of riding every mood around you. Whenever you hold steady by choice, not from habit, you keep some of that calm for yourself.
angles.cost_self: Holding steady for everyone, you hide your worst days. You absorb a bad day instead of naming it, and it settles in your body as tiredness. Tell one friend about a rough week, to take in some of the comfort you give everyone else.
angles.cost_others: Good news or bad, you hold steady and look the same. You would sooner keep a level face than show a peer what you feel. When you let one peer see what moves you, you stop leaving them to guess what matters.

angles.drive: Whatever the problem, you never ask for help. Needing someone feels like weakness, and you work it out alone instead of handing any of it over. Keep in mind that anything you never ask about stays yours for longer than it needs to.
angles.cost_self: Pride stays whole when you never ask, and so do your problems. You carry what a quick question would have halved, since being seen needing something hurts more than the weight does. Remember that you lose sleep over what one question would have settled.
angles.cost_others: By never asking, you take something from those who would have said yes. You would rather show up than need someone, and you only show your friends the half that is fine. You only ever let someone in by letting them help.

angles.drive: Tired, you shut people out before anything else. Quiet is how you recover, and you shut people out sooner than ask for the quiet you need. The longer you shut people out to rest, the harder you find the way back.
angles.cost_self: Where you shut people out, you shut out what you were saving yourself for. Your own company works so well that you mistake it for the plan rather than a break. You pay for that peace in closeness, one quiet evening at a time.
angles.cost_others: You mostly shut out people who did nothing to earn it. You keep to yourself rather than explain yourself, and you hand a friend your distance before your reason. Bear in mind how long you leave people waiting for a welcome you rarely give.

angles.drive: You take no advice you have not tested yourself. Catching your own mistakes matters more to you than having a peer point them out. You do not have to be wrong to take advice that makes your plan better.
angles.cost_self: With no advice taken, you learn at full price. Whenever you would rather learn a thing yourself than be told, a friend's one sentence becomes your whole season. You end up repeating mistakes a friend had already solved for you.
angles.cost_others: When a friend offers advice, you thank them and go your own way. You keep your own plan ahead of theirs, and the care they put in goes to waste. Notice that taking even one piece of their advice tells them their care landed.

angles.drive: You are better with a rival in sight. Your own pace never quite wakes you, so you measure yourself against a person rather than a plan. Pick your rivals on purpose, and you turn a reflex into the fastest way you grow.
angles.cost_self: Being better with rivals leaves you rarely at your best alone. Without someone to beat, you drift rather than push, so the goals only you care about wait longest. Find a rival for the private goals too, and you stop leaving your own for last.
angles.cost_others: Better with a rival, you turn a peer into one without asking. You would rather race someone than keep them company, and you hand a contest to a friend who wanted none. Name the race, and you give them the choice to run it.

angles.drive: You bet big because only a real stake gets all of you, and you would rather risk a lot on one move than a little on many. If you let small bets count too, you stop missing the gains that come slowly.
angles.cost_self: Where you bet big, you lose at the same size. You stake the whole amount instead of keeping some in reserve. When you hold back one part of each bet, you keep the savings a single loss would take.
angles.cost_others: On a shared stake, you bet someone else's year with your own. You would rather win it all for both of you than keep half safe, and their caution becomes your dare. Ask first, because you keep a partner who chose the risk.

angles.drive: With a win in hand, you would rather share the credit than keep it, because a prize means more with your people inside it. When a win can count before you have shared it, you get to enjoy it twice.
angles.cost_self: Taking the credit alone feels like showing off to you. You hand out credit rather than keep it, and your own work goes unnamed. If you put your own name on your part, you stop losing the chances that follow credit.
angles.cost_others: The credit you share lands on people who did not run for it. You would rather have company at the finish than stand there alone, and you pass out what only you earned. Name who did what, to give praise each person can use.

angles.drive: In new company, you are comparing before you have said much. A clear rank makes you feel safe, and you compare yourself to someone rather than get to know them. Once the ranking is done, you have often missed the person.
angles.cost_self: Always comparing gives you a result and never rest. You would rather know where you rank than enjoy where you are, so no win gets time to feel like one. You lose the quiet of a good week to a score only you can see.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a friend has good news, you compare before you say well done. You measure the gap ahead of being glad for them, and you give less praise than they earned. You can let their news stay theirs for a day and compare later.

angles.drive: You feel every loss as a blow to your standing. You would rather sit out a contest than risk losing it, because your standing feels at stake. Remember that you are beaten far less often than you think, and you keep every one.
angles.cost_self: Hating to lose costs you the losses that would have taught you most. You would rather not play than be beaten, and you never enter the contests with the most to teach you. You protect a record with very few wins on it.
angles.cost_others: Shared things turn into contests when you hate to lose. You would rather win the argument than keep the evening, and you put a friend on the losing side of a game they never entered. You leave with the point and a little less warmth.

angles.drive: As a contest gets close, you spend to win it. You would rather pay to stay ahead than risk falling behind, and you spend to prove a point. Ask yourself before you pay whether you want the thing or only the win.
angles.cost_self: Where you spend to win, you end up with the win and without the money. You would rather look ahead of a rival than quietly stay ahead, so the savings go on rounds nobody asked for. You notice the money you did not keep last.
angles.cost_others: To win, you spend what is not only yours. You would rather cover the whole bill than split it, and you spend money your partner set aside for the two of you. You spend the trust in a shared account faster than the balance.

angles.drive: Giving comes to you before the question does. Being useful is how you feel you belong, so you give first rather than wait to be asked. You lose nothing by waiting for the question, since a gift asked for is the one that gets kept.
angles.cost_self: Before the asking, you have usually already given. Because the gift comes ahead of the need, you never learn whether you were wanted or only useful. You pay in a closeness you never get to test until you let the asking come first.
angles.cost_others: Giving first is your way of saying you noticed. Each time you give instead of waiting to be needed, you take from the people closest to you the small pride of asking. Leave them the asking along with the giving.

angles.drive: What you make is made to last, slowly and on purpose. The making itself is the enjoyment, so you make things for the years rather than for the showing. You deserve the showing as much as the making, because work that stays unseen stays unused.
angles.cost_self: Making things last is your idea of doing something right. Since the work is only right once it holds, you would rather be finished than first. Show one thing before it is done, or the chances that wanted you early close while you keep making.
angles.cost_others: You make things last for your family rather than arrive on time. You never count the waiting, and next year you deliver what was needed this year. You are free to hand over an early version, and a thing used now beats one admired later.

angles.drive: Enough is a place you can live in. Being happy with what is here comes easier than wanting, so you enjoy what you have rather than chase what you lack. Let yourself want more sometimes, because enough has a way of shrinking.
angles.cost_self: Being happy with enough spares you a lot of chasing. Because contentment feels like wisdom, you settle for what is here instead of asking for more. Ask for more once a year, since the chance you never test closes as quietly as you settled.
angles.cost_others: At home, enough is the mood you set. Whenever enough comes early for you, you settle for the people in your care rather than push for them. Want more out loud for them, and the size of your enough becomes the size of their life.

angles.drive: Giving is the one thing you never run out of. Since being useful feels more like you than being rested, you keep giving after the supply behind it goes quiet. Keep in mind that the giving lasts only as long as you do.
angles.cost_self: Giving without stopping is how you avoid asking what you need. Because running low feels better than asking, you give the rest you needed to whoever is next in line. Remember that the rest you keep skipping is the supply the giving runs on.
angles.cost_others: You give to the people at home without stopping, and never leave them a turn. Since giving feels safer than needing, you take from them the chance to look after you. You owe them the closeness of giving back once in a while.

angles.drive: Drifting along is comfortable, and comfort is enough for you. Since the easy day never argues and the hard start always does, you would rather drift than start. You will want to remember that drifting feels like rest until it costs you what you wanted.
angles.cost_self: Drifting along is your way around deciding anything. Because the comfortable day is already here, you keep choosing it instead of making the better one. You let the chance you were good enough for close while you drift, and you rarely count it.
angles.cost_others: Drifting along at home means the steering is not yours. Since going with the day suits you more than setting it, you leave the people you live with the choices you skip. You hand them the weight with the choice, and that is worth remembering.

angles.drive: Going soft on the people around you comes to you without thinking. Since comfort is the shape your care takes, you soften their way rather than let them manage it. Remember that a little struggle is also something you can give.
angles.cost_self: Being too soft is how you say you care. Because you put other people's comfort ahead of anything kept for yourself, you go soft over money and spend what you set aside. You know the money and rest you give away do not come back.
angles.cost_others: You go soft on whoever is in your care because their struggle hurts. Since you fix their trouble rather than sit through it, you go soft before the first try ends. You keep taking from them a struggle that was theirs to grow on.

angles.drive: Proving a point matters more to you than making it. Because a finished thing argues better than you could out loud, you would rather prove an idea than pitch it. You pay in time, and you get to be right in a way that lasts.
angles.cost_self: Proving it is the only kind of winning you trust. Since you prove rather than pitch, you let the chances that needed a quick yes go by. You lose credit for ideas that were yours first, so pitch one before the proof is done.
angles.cost_others: You prove an idea before you share it. Whenever you would rather show a result than explain a plan, you keep people out of it until it is done. Tell one person the plan early, since a surprise is harder to help than a sketch.

angles.drive: Speaking plainly comes easier to you than softening it. Since a true thing said flat feels more honest than a kind thing dressed up, you speak plainly rather than nicely. You pay for it in warmth, and to you the truth is worth it.
angles.cost_self: Speaking plainly is how you stay honest with yourself. You would rather be understood than liked, so you say what goes unsaid and give up the easy welcome of keeping quiet. Soften one true thing a week, because you wanted that welcome too.
angles.cost_others: You speak plainly to the people who matter most to you. Where the truth counts for more than the landing, you hand it over without the cushion it needed. Add the cushion sometimes, because you want them to land softly too.

angles.drive: Rules read to you as first drafts. Since you would rather fix a bad rule than follow it, you rewrite it in the doing and in plain sight. You spend a while being marked wrong, and the rewrite tends to look like sense later.
angles.cost_self: Rewriting a rule is your answer to one that makes no sense. Each time you choose to fix it rather than obey it, you lose the credit that following it would earn. Follow one you dislike this month, because that approval was yours too.
angles.cost_others: You rewrite a rule that stops making sense under the people standing on it. Since you fix it ahead of keeping the peace, you change the footing with no warning. Give the warning first, because the rule you found pointless was somebody's floor.

angles.drive: Pushing back is your first reply to almost anything. Because agreeing feels like giving something up, you push against a plan rather than check if you mind it. Keep in mind, pushing back costs you the same whether the plan was good or not.
angles.cost_self: Pushing back is how you keep hold of yourself in a group. Since giving in feels like disappearing, you push against help as much as against orders. Remember that what you keep pushing away is help you needed.
angles.cost_others: You push back before you hear the end of a plan. Where being hard to convince feels like being hard to fool, you make people defend a plan instead of taking it. You cost them the ease of offering, and you know it.

angles.drive: Saying too much is the honesty you were built for. A thought left unsaid feels like a lie to you, so you say the whole thing rather than the useful half. Remember that the useful half was the only part you were asked for.
angles.cost_self: Saying too much proves to you that you were listening. Since a held tongue feels like a wasted turn, you spend your standing on the extra line instead of the needed one. You know the trust you talk away comes back slower than it left.
angles.cost_others: You say too much to whoever let you speak. Because a thought feels wasted unless it is said, you take their turn as much as your own. You owe whoever you talked over the sentence you took.

angles.drive: Overdoing it is the only way you know to be sure of enough. Since plain and finished feels like settling, you make it bigger rather than call it done. You pay for the extra out of yourself, a price worth keeping in mind.
angles.cost_self: Overdoing it is how you make sure a thing looks like you. Long after the plain version would do, you keep adding rather than finishing and spend what the end needed. You pay for every extra in the sleep the finish was owed.
angles.cost_others: You overdo it for people who asked for something modest. Since a plain job feels beneath what you can do, you hand them a bigger thing later instead of the small thing now. You owed them the small one now, the one with a use.

angles.drive: You see a chance long before anyone else wants it. Having somewhere next to go is your safety, so you watch where a thing is heading more than what it is. Looking far costs you some of what is near, and the trade favors you.
angles.cost_self: Looking far comes naturally, and it pays. The next place is clearer to you than this one, so you see the far chance sooner than the near one. You lose the opening at hand most, and one quick look before passing it keeps it.
angles.cost_others: You look past the people closest to you toward the next place. Seeing far is how you keep them safe, and that gives the plan more of you than them. If you let them look with you, you see far enough for all of them.

angles.drive: A chance within reach is hard to leave alone, because standing in place feels like losing. You take the one that is here rather than wait for a safer one. You take them best with your eyes open, since some of them cost you.
angles.cost_self: Taking the chance pays you more than waiting does. Moving makes you feel alive, so you put money into what moves rather than what is safe. Take the next one with money you can spare, because the wrong ones cost what the sure ones kept.
angles.cost_others: You take the chance for everyone whose money sits beside yours. Moving feels safer to you than staying, and you put their calm into the venture with your own. You take it for them too, and choosing its size with them costs you nothing.

angles.drive: A win only feels real to you once you have shared it. Providing is where you feel most yourself, and you share a good month rather than put it away. You share because it is right for you, and the thinner cushion is the price.
angles.cost_self: Sharing the win is your natural generosity, and it leaves you short. What you give in a good year you lack in a lean one, because giving comes ahead of keeping. If you keep some of each win back, the lean year stops costing you.
angles.cost_others: You share each win rather than sit on it. Giving in bursts is your way of loving, and you hand them plenty one year and nothing the next. You do them more good sharing in a shape that lasts, since they come back.

angles.drive: The next chance always looks better to you than the one in your hands. Movement is how you feel alive, and you chase what is coming rather than work what is here. Keep in mind that you only keep what you stay to collect.
angles.cost_self: Chasing the next chance costs you the one you hold now. Each new start takes the strength the last one needs, and you would rather begin again than finish. You already know that the chance in your hands closes while you are off chasing.
angles.cost_others: You chase the next chance before anyone is out of the last one. You want starting more than staying, and you give the new venture what you owed the old one. Try to remember that you leave someone holding each chance you chase past.

angles.drive: You are spread across more things than any one of them can use. Saying no feels like losing, so you hold many small pieces rather than one whole thing. You give each one a part and none the whole, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_self: Spreading yourself thin keeps you from being caught out and keeps you tired. You give each venture enough to stay in rather than enough to win, since quitting feels like losing. Remember that you pay for all of them with the one body you have.
angles.cost_others: Wherever you can reach, you spread yourself across every person and plan. Keeping every option alive matters more to you than giving one your whole attention. Do not forget that you give each person in your plans the part of you the others left.

angles.drive: Starting a thing gives you more than finishing it. The beginning is where the feeling lives, and you spend your strength there rather than on the last stretch. You get nothing for the half until the rest is done, and you need no reminding.
angles.cost_self: Finishing is what you save for later. The last stretch costs you more than the first, and you open a new thing sooner than you close an old one. Hold onto the thought that the money and the credit sit at the end you leave.
angles.cost_others: You hand people a beginning and call it done. Starting is where you feel strongest, and you put everything into the first stretch instead of saving some for the last. Make a note that you give the people waiting your start and somebody else's finish.

angles.drive: Making a thing last is a craft you practice without noticing. Waste feels to you like a small loss of control, so you repair what you own rather than replace it. You pay by living with the older version a while longer than you need.
angles.cost_self: Making things last keeps you in control of what you own. You put hours into repairs ahead of the better thing on offer, because replacing feels like waste. Once fixing costs more than the thing is worth, letting it go gives you those hours back.
angles.cost_others: You keep old things going for everyone around you. Fixing beats choosing for you, and you have the people at home living with your kept things rather than their own. You make the rest last, and one new thing a year is theirs to pick.

angles.drive: Saving comes first for you, ahead of the treat and the trip. A cushion is what lets you relax, and you put money away rather than enjoy it. Saving first suits you, and a few good things you were slow to buy are the price.
angles.cost_self: Saving first is the quiet skill under everything you own. You would rather be covered than pleased, and the good thing you can afford keeps waiting. If you spend one saved sum on something you want, the pleasure you put off stops being the price.
angles.cost_others: You save for the people you love ahead of spending on them. A safe future is the gift you trust, and you give them the cushion rather than the dinner. Spend part of it on them this year, because it was for them all along.

angles.drive: Being loyal costs you less than leaving ever would. The known thing keeps you safe, and you hold what is already yours instead of looking elsewhere. You stay a while past where it serves you, and that is the price of loyalty like yours.
angles.cost_self: Your loyalty stays put, and it pays in people who stay. You keep choosing what is yours rather than ask if it chooses you too. Asking every so often costs you little, while loyalty to what does not love you back costs you closeness.
angles.cost_others: Loyalty is how you love, shown by staying. You keep the one you have rather than look around, and you let the staying speak for you. Being chosen again is a thing you give out loud, and you give it less than you mean to.

angles.drive: Letting a thing go is harder for you than keeping it. Having it within reach makes you feel safe, so you keep things for a someday need rather than a present use. Tell yourself plainly that everything you keep also has to be looked after.
angles.cost_self: Keeping everything is your insurance against going without, and it costs you. You would rather pay to store a thing than risk needing it, and your money guards what you never use. Let yourself see that you rent space for things that give nothing back.
angles.cost_others: You hold onto things you cannot bring yourself to drop. You keep a thing rather than take its space back, and you fill the home from the walls in. Keep sight of how you charge the people at home for it in space.

angles.drive: Staying put feels like safety, whatever the place becomes. Moving asks more of you than staying, so you keep the known rather than go toward the better. Know that a place you will not leave is not one that holds you.
angles.cost_self: Being hard to move keeps your life steady and small. You would rather weigh a move than make one, and the better place is taken while you weigh it. Take it as given that the chance to go closes during the deciding.
angles.cost_others: You stay, and hold the people closest to you in place. Staying matters to you more than moving somewhere better together, and you set the whole house to your speed. Ask yourself whether you make them wait on a move you are not making.

angles.drive: You hate to spend, even on the things you can plainly afford. Spending feels like losing control, and you hold onto the money rather than buy what you wanted. Be honest with yourself about how much more you can afford than you let yourself have.
angles.cost_self: Hating to spend means you rarely overpay and rarely enjoy. You would rather keep the money than spend it, since spending feels like a loss already begun. Keep it in view that you end up with the money and without the thing it was for.
angles.cost_others: Spending on the people you love comes no easier than spending on yourself. Giving less feels safer than giving more, and you make the saving on them. Spare a thought for what you save on them, since it comes out of their side.

angles.drive: You stay calm under pressure, and it shows. Pressure hands you something solid to hold, and you save your calm for the hard moment ahead of the ordinary day. When a quiet day comes, give it some calm too, because that calm is yours anyway.
angles.cost_self: Whenever pressure comes on, you turn calm. You spend that calm on a crisis ahead of an ordinary week, and the ordinary weeks get skipped. If you keep one stretch clear of crisis, you find that the calm comes with you, the rest with it.
angles.cost_others: Your calm is what you offer first in a crisis. You would rather carry the hard part for someone than watch them shake, and you take it off their hands before their calm gets a chance. Let someone else stay calm beside you for once.

angles.drive: Taking charge is a reflex for you. You would rather own a wrong call than leave one with no owner, and you take charge before anyone asks. If you hand a few calls to someone else, taking charge goes back to being a choice.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a plan stalls, you take charge, wanted or not. Deciding feels like safety to you, more than waiting ever does, and calls that were never yours end up with you. When you turn one down, you keep the evening it would have eaten.
angles.cost_others: For you, looking after a group means taking charge of it. Handing people an answer comes easier to you than waiting while they find one, and the finding is what you take from them. Leave one call open long enough for someone else to make.

angles.drive: Pushing through is how you get to the end of anything hard. You need something to push against, and you finish under strain more easily than at ease. Push on, and notice which jobs you only finish when something pushes back.
angles.cost_self: Under strain, you push through without a second thought. You would sooner push to the far side than ask for less, and you never try the lighter road. Make one job easy on purpose, and keep the strength that pushing costs.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you push through, you carry the people with you at your pace. You would rather hold the pace than slow it for someone, and that costs them the pause you never take. When you match the slowest once, you see what gets done anyway.

angles.drive: Being hard on yourself is the pressure you never question. Before anyone outside can judge you, you have judged yourself, and you would sooner be hard on yourself than hear it from them. You pay for getting there first in sleep you never get back.
angles.cost_self: Once a job is done, you are hard on yourself about the part that fell short. You would rather judge your own work than let anyone else, and the praise never gets in. It is worth remembering that you leave the credit you earned unspent.
angles.cost_others: You stay hard on yourself in front of the people you love. Getting it right comes first, ahead of being easy company, so each kindness you refuse teaches them to keep theirs. You teach them your harshness without ever meaning it for them.

angles.drive: You are never off duty, even when nothing needs guarding. To you standing down is a drop in rank rather than a rest, and quiet weeks get watched like hard ones. Keep in mind that you skip real sleep to guard nothing.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the work ends, you find a reason to stay on duty. You trust being needed more than being free, until a day off turns into a day waiting for a call. You refuse the rest that no one else can take for you.
angles.cost_others: You come home on duty, and your family gets the guard rather than the person. Keeping watch feels more useful than being there, and your attention goes to the next problem. Do not forget that you were wanted off duty more than on it.

angles.drive: You shut people out before they get close enough to press on you. Since your own pressure is plenty, shutting out anyone else's feels like safety rather than loss. Try to remember that shutting out the pressure shuts out the closeness with it.
angles.cost_self: Where help is offered, you shut it out kindly. You want no one pressing on you more than anyone helping, and what was meant for two gets carried by one. You end up paying alone for every hand you turned away.
angles.cost_others: Reaching for you is pressure too, and you shut out the people who try. You would rather be alone than understood, and the door shuts hardest on those closest. You leave them outside with no reason and no way to ask for one.

angles.drive: You keep every promise, including the ones that stopped making sense. Your word is what you stand on, and keeping it matters more to you than whether the promise fits your life now. If you change one promise out loud, you keep the rest whole.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you give your word, you keep the promise in full. You wear reliable better than happy, and the agreements that cost more each year stay put. When you change one out loud, you get the plan you gave up for it back.
angles.cost_others: Long after you stopped wanting to, you keep promises to people. Holding counts for more with you than honesty about changing, and you never tell the person that the promise went stale. Give one person the real answer, and let them choose.

angles.drive: You play fair even when it costs you the win. You only trust a rule that applies to everyone, and you keep yourself to it rather than make yourself the exception. If you let one person see the fairness, you lose nothing.
angles.cost_self: Where a shortcut gets you ahead, you play fair and arrive late. Being right with yourself comes ahead of arriving first, and the quick wins go to people who care less. Claim what you earned fairly, because the title you wait on goes elsewhere.
angles.cost_others: With the people closest to you, you play fair exactly as with strangers. Being fair to everyone comes ahead of being on anyone's side, and you never pick theirs either. Make one small exception, and see how little fairness it costs.

angles.drive: You set the standard before anyone asks for one. You would rather set a clear standard than argue over one, and the one you set binds you first. When you set one with people instead of for them, you share its weight.
angles.cost_self: Wherever a standard is missing, you set one and live under it. You take your own bar as the measure ahead of anyone else's, and yours sits a step above you. If you set the bar where you stand, you pass it for once.
angles.cost_others: You set a standard for the whole group. You hold people to a standard they can see rather than guess at, and the standard you set is theirs to meet too. If you ask them where to set it, you find it met more gladly.

angles.drive: You follow every rule, including the ones nobody checks. You like knowing where you stand more than deciding for yourself, and you follow rules written for someone else too. You pay for that sureness with decisions that were yours to make.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a rule and a chance pull apart, you follow the rule. Order weighs more than luck with you, and the chances that need a rule stretched pass you by. It helps to remember that you hand those openings to rules nobody checks.
angles.cost_others: You follow rules even with the people who need an exception. You find fair by the book easier than kind off it, and you hand them policy instead of a decision. You give them your rulebook and keep your judgment to yourself.

angles.drive: You wait for permission to take what is already yours. You trust an approval from above more than your own certainty, and you sit on a plan until someone signs it. You give the plan's best months to waiting, and that is worth noticing.
angles.cost_self: Where a raise is there for the asking, you wait for permission. You count a handed thing as more earned than a claimed one, and you wait on an offer waiting on you. You lose the raise you never ask for, year after year.
angles.cost_others: You wait for permission for everyone waiting on you. Being cleared from above sits better with you than moving on your own say, and you keep the people behind you waiting. Hold on to the fact that you hand your wait to them without asking.

angles.drive: You are slow to change, and slow on purpose. You trust what has held more than anything untested, and a new way earns years before it gets a week. It bears remembering that staying put costs you the years a better way would have given.
angles.cost_self: Whenever something needs changing, you change it last. You would sooner keep what you know than find out what else there is, and you stay in a job you stopped liking for years. Remember how you spend each deciding year staying put.
angles.cost_others: Even for those who need you to, you change slowly. Changing for one person feels less fair to you than keeping things the same, and you keep that person waiting. Keep sight of how you make them live the old way while you decide.

angles.drive: Teaching yourself matters more to you than being taught. Needing to understand before you trust, you teach yourself from odd sources rather than take the standard lesson. Let someone teach you from time to time, since a lesson only you know is lonely.
